title: NY State Assembly · District 80
area: The Bronx: Allerton, Morris Park, Norwood, Pelham Gardens, Pelham Parkway, and Van Nest

context.text: Both parties' primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026 were canceled. Incumbent John Zaccaro Jr. (D) advanced without appearing on the ballot. Denise Smith withdrew from the Republican primary but advanced from the Conservative Party primary without appearing on the ballot, so she appears on the Conservative Party line only.

summary.text: John Zaccaro Jr. is the incumbent Democratic Assembly Member for District 80 in the Bronx, seeking his third term. He previously served as Chief of Staff to a New York City Council member and as a tenant-rights housing organizer.

background.text: Zaccaro was born and raised in the Bronx by a single mother and has described experiencing housing insecurity growing up.

He began his career as an intern for the New York City Council, then worked as a housing organizer helping residents fight poor living conditions and unwarranted rent increases and working with community groups to challenge landlords in court.

He served as Bronx Director for Intergovernmental Affairs under New York City Schools Chancellor Carmen Fariña, and later as Chief of Staff for City Councilmember Rafael Salamanca before his election to the Assembly.

As of the 2025-2026 session, he sits on the Assembly's Aging, Alcoholism and Drug Abuse, Economic Development/Job Creation/Commerce and Industry, Education, Small Business, and Tourism/Parks/Arts and Sports Development committees.

priorities.text: "In just three years, he has helped secure millions in funding and advance legislation that strengthens neighborhoods across the district," with investments listed in schools and youth programs, housing stability and senior services, community safety and mental health resources, and parks and local business corridors.

Looking ahead, his stated priorities include expanding after-school programs and school-to-career pathways, protecting Mitchell-Lama housing and supporting homeowners and tenants, investing in community-based public-safety and mental-health services, expanding senior services, and improving city and state agency responsiveness.

He announced that the 2024 state budget included new enforcement powers to revoke the tobacco, liquor, or lottery licenses of businesses that possess or sell illegal cannabis, which he described as a win against illegal smoke shops in his district.

record.text: Announced that the state budget signed in April 2024 gave localities new enforcement powers to revoke tobacco, liquor, or lottery licenses from businesses selling illegal cannabis, targeting unlicensed smoke shops in his district.
Voted yes on S10113, which passed the Assembly 88–53, allowing a cannabis microbusiness licensee authorized for retail sales to also serve as a processor and cultivator for cannabis showcase events.
Voted yes on S3460, which passed the Assembly 92–49, granting employees access to their personnel records and requiring notice and a review opportunity for negative information in those records.

As of the 2025-2026 session, serves on the Assembly's Aging, Alcoholism and Drug Abuse, Economic Development/Job Creation/Commerce and Industry, Education, Small Business, and Tourism/Parks/Arts and Sports Development committees.

summary.text: Denise Smith is the Conservative Party candidate for Assembly District 80. She ran unsuccessfully for New York City Council District 11 on the Conservative Party line in 2025.

background.text: In the November 2025 general election for New York City Council District 11, Smith received 4.0% of the vote (1,462 votes) on the Conservative Party line, behind incumbent Eric Dinowitz (D) and Stylo A. Sapaskis (R).
